sites.name: Project Washington (Starwood Digital Ventures)
sites.note: DNREC Secretary denied Coastal Zone Act permit February 4, 2026 citing 516 backup diesel generators and 2.5 million gallons of stored diesel as unprecedented heavy industrial use under Delaware's 1971 Coastal Zone Act. sites.name: Murray Industries Pineville Data Center
sites.note: Hundreds of residents filled the old courthouse in Pineville for a June 26, 2026 special-called fiscal court meeting to oppose the project over water quality, noise and road impacts; the fiscal court gave first reading to a moratorium that day and passed a two-year ban on data center construction in July 2026. Residents subsequently reported that land-clearing work continued despite the moratorium.

sites.name: Panattoni Burgin Data Center Campus
sites.note: National developer Panattoni's proposed hyperscale AI data center on unincorporated farmland near Burgin would require annexation of 1,000+ acres, roughly doubling Burgin's size. About 200 residents attended a Mercer County Planning & Zoning Commission hearing on 2026-07-30 (commission voted unanimously to advance data-center-enabling regulations the same day); the Burgin city council had voted 3-2 for a first reading of the annexation ordinance in early July 2026. Grassroots group 'We Are Mercer County' formed with 1,000+ Facebook members; residents wore blue 'no data center' shirts. Resident Stacey Sellers: 'Please, do not let the greed of a few outweigh the wellbeing of our people.' Mercer County Fiscal Court passed a one-year moratorium on 2026-08-12 that explicitly exempts Burgin's pending annexation; residents packed Burgin city hall that day in opposition. Resident Beth Corea: 'They want our land, our water, our electricity.'

sites.name: PowerHouse Data Centers – Louisville (Camp Ground Road)
sites.note: Strong community opposition from Rubbertown-area residents citing energy affordability burdens on low-income customers, environmental and health equity concerns in a historically underserved West End neighborhood. Multiple public hearings with significant protests. Louisville Party for Socialism and Liberation among opponents.

sites.name: Carrollton Industrial Campus
sites.note: Carroll County/Ghent-area residents organized opposition (group 'No Data Center 502') after learning the Carrollton Industrial Campus had reportedly been in development for over a year before its public announcement. Reporting says the Carrollton mayor signed an unrecorded real estate option contract in July 2025 to sell 340 acres of public land for the project. Residents cite lack of transparency: 'There's been no transparency from our local government' (Laura Beth Austin); 'I don't trust the jobs numbers. I don't trust the tax numbers' (Amy Wright). State Sen. Gex Williams (R) said the city 'made some serious mistakes in terms of their NDAs'; Sen. Keturah Herron (D) said 'If you are not being open and honest ... then we can only assume that it's shady business happening.' A Kentucky State Senate District 20 candidate (Stella Pollard) and the Louisville group opposing a separate PowerHouse/Poe project have joined the organizing.

sites.name: Rubix Ashland Works Data Center Campus
sites.note: The City of Russell passed a six-month moratorium on the construction and operation of data centers within city limits in June 2026. Rubix answered a city due-diligence questionnaire and scheduled a public meeting with county officials and residents.

Developer Dennis Griffin said data centers were being treated 'very, very unfairly.'

The commission also recommended a six-month moratorium on data-center development.
